prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
The API now requires API keys with viewer, cook and manager roles. Missing or unknown keys get a 401 `unauthorized` error and keys without permission get a 403 `forbidden` error. Every non-GET request made with a known key is written to the audit log, and managers can read it newest first at `GET /audit`. Both `npm test` (30 tests) and `npm run lint` pass.

Things you might not expect:
- **Schema bumped to 3.** Adding keys and the audit log changes the data format, so I added a migration. Older data files open with no keys, which means every request to them gets 401 until keys are added.
- **One CLI test changed.** Because of the bump, the `larder migrate` test now expects schema 3 instead of 2.
- **`data/db.json` overwritten.** It was identical to the seed file, so I replaced it with the new seed. Without that, `npm start` would reject every request. It now holds the three development keys, which shouldn't go to production.
- **What gets logged.** The log keeps every outcome, including refused (403) and failed requests, because it records the status. Requests rejected with 401 are not logged, so anyone without a key can't fill up the log.

Existing tests now send the manager key by default through `tests/helpers.js`. New tests in `tests/access.test.js` cover the 401 and 403 responses, what each role can do, and the audit log. The docs and changelog are updated.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
